newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close stronger, aided by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close stronger, aided by bonds.

text.p: * Toronto stocks closed firmer on a stronger bond market, resisting the late afternoon downturn in New York and softer golds. * 105 million shares traded worth C$1.48 billion.
The Toronto stock market followed a rally in bonds to end stronger on Friday, resisting the late afternoon downturn in New York and weakness in the heavily weighted gold sector.
Toronto's key stock index rose 24.48 points to hit 6109.58, within sight of its all-time high of 6144.29 reached on January 17. Turnover was moderate at 105 million shares worth C$1.48 billion.
"It's the strength in the bond market and the bill market," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie. Canada's benchmark 30-year bond jumped C$1.20 to C$109.15.

North American bonds rallied after U.S. gross domestic product numbers this morning suggested inflation is not accelerating. This eased worries the U.S. Federal Reserve members will tighten short-term interest rates at next week's meeting.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, only four slipped -- key golds, conglomerates, transports and base metals. The stronger side was led by retail, pipelines, forestry products and consumer products.
Advancing issues outstripped declining ones 539 to 436, while 290 traded unchanged.
Toronto, Canada's largest equities market, gained 80 points during the week from Monday's low of 6029.94.

* Mitel Corp dropped 0.85 to 9.85 on more than 2.4 million shares after reporting third quarter earnings below the consensus reached by analysts. Profit was flat at C$0.10 a share versus the same a year earlier.
Yesterday the telecommunications firm forecast expanded business in Mexico.
